scope.note: PROVENANCE: the light value is measured off .impeccable/mocks/decision/assigned.png, a decision-round comp never approved as the comp of record, with no re-derivation ruling covering it (unlike this file's other light-theme values, which carry an explicit M1-11 ruling). Kept because it is the only measurement on hand, not because its provenance was cleared.

label.purpose: Captions, field labels, plate labels, nav.

figure.purpose: Any number or identifier that lines up in a column; tabular-nums, one size per call site.

code.purpose: TOML bodies, log lines, transcripts, file paths — genuinely monospace content only.

shadows.name: strip-border-lip
shadows.value: border: 1px solid color-mix(in srgb, var(--strip) 76%, white)
shadows.purpose: The paper's own brighter inner lip, part of the three-ring paper edge.

shadows.name: strip-outline-ring
shadows.purpose: Mid-tone shade ring, one step out from the strip border.

shadows.name: strip-room-ring
shadows.purpose: Darkest outline ring, mixed against the plane (bay) it sits on so it needs no per-theme hex.

shadows.name: bay-inset-ring
shadows.value: box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 1px color-mix(in srgb, var(--room) 27%, black)
shadows.purpose: The recessed frame of a rack.

motion.name: dur-1
motion.purpose: Border/background hover transitions (key hover, edge mark).

motion.name: dur-2
motion.purpose: The one authored entrance: a phone-mode swell fading and translating in.

components.name: Key (Button)
components.description: A printed strip that can be pressed. Hover lifts only the border color; focus is the world's 2px ring.
components.css: .ds-key { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 4px; padding: 4px 8px; background: #DED9C6; color: #141414; border: 1px solid #A8A392; border-radius: 0; font-family: Archivo, 'Helvetica Neue', Arial, sans-serif; font-size: 0.875rem; cursor: pointer; transition: border-color 120ms cubic-bezier(.22,1,.36,1); } .ds-key:hover { border-color: #141414; } .ds-key:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #3F76B4; outline-offset: 1px; }

components.name: Key Armed (Confirm)
components.description: The second half of a two-step destructive key: paper steps up one rung and a filled danger tint arrives so a scan of the bench cannot mistake it for the idle stop control.
components.css: .ds-key-armed { border-color: #141414; background: #E4E0D1; color: #E63521; } .ds-key-armed::before { content: ''; display: inline-block; width: 4px; align-self: stretch; background: #E63521; margin-inline-end: 4px; }

components.name: StripField
components.description: A boxed record cell: a mute label 4px above a hairline, a tabular value 4px below it, fixed ch width.
components.css: .ds-sfield { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 4px; padding: 4px 8px 12px; background: #E4E0D1; border-inline-end: 1px solid #A8A392; font-family: 'JetBrains Mono', ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, monospace; } .ds-sfield-label { font-size: 0.75rem; color: #5A5749; border-bottom: 1px solid #5A5749; } .ds-sfield-value { font-size: 1rem; color: #141414; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; }

components.name: HolderEdge
components.description: The only place attention is carried by color; always paired with its own text label, never color alone.
components.css: .ds-edge { display: inline-flex; align-items: stretch; gap: 4px; } .ds-edge-mark { width: 4px; background: #6E6D68; } .ds-edge-green .ds-edge-mark { background: #548630; } .ds-edge-label { font-family: Archivo, sans-serif; font-size: 0.75rem; color: inherit; }

components.name: Field Input
components.description: A strip's field box with a caret: same paper, hairline and radius as a StripField, figure face for the value.
components.css: .ds-input { display: inline-flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 2px; } .ds-input-label { font-family: Archivo, sans-serif; font-size: 0.75rem; color: #5A5749; } .ds-input-box { padding: 4px 8px; background: #E4E0D1; color: #141414; border: 1px solid #A8A392; border-radius: 0; font-family: Archivo, sans-serif; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; font-size: 1rem; } .ds-input-box:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #3F76B4; outline-offset: 1px; }

components.name: Bay Head Plate
components.description: The bolted head plate over a rack, carrying a live label, a count, and the rack's actions at its right end.
components.css: .ds-bay-head { display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: 4px; width: max-content; padding: 4px 8px; background-color: #C3B6A0; color: #141414; border: 1px solid color-mix(in srgb, #C3B6A0 76%, white); box-shadow: 0 0 0 1px #645F50; } .ds-bay-label { font-family: Archivo, sans-serif; font-size: 1.0625rem; color: #141414; } .ds-bay-count { font-family: Archivo, sans-serif; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; font-size: 0.75rem; color: color-mix(in srgb, #141414 95%, #C3B6A0); }

narrative.overview: The console is a rack in a graphite room: opaque paper strips racked in steel bays, each strip a printed record — an account, a head, a turn — carrying a colored holder edge that flags its state. Nothing floats and nothing glows. A value is a printed figure in a boxed field, a label is mute ink above a hairline, and the only saturated color in the frame is the holder edge itself, because the world's one rule is that attention is a color and everything else is graphite and paper. PRODUCT.md's own voice — "terse, lowercase, data-first... the loudest thing on screen is a real warning" — is the strip bay's whole brief: this is an instrument panel for one operator glancing between terminal sessions, not a marketing surface. This system explicitly rejects the KPI-tile dashboard: no hero metric rendered at a jump in size, no sparkline or progress ring standing in for content, no card-and-shadow SaaS vocabulary. It also retired an entire earlier world (the "Torad plate" system: warm paper, cinnabar/vermilion accent, serif numerals) — that world is gone from the shipped build; nothing in this document should be read against it.
keyCharacteristics: Flat, radius-0 paper-on-graphite construction; depth by tonal plane and hairline, never shadow.
One functional accent per state (the holder edge's green/amber/red/grey); no second accent color anywhere in the room.
Two faces only: a label/figure grotesque (Archivo, tabular figures) and a monospace for genuinely code-shaped content (JetBrains Mono).
A light-dark()-driven root scalar ties root font size to the frame's own width, so the console is the comp's render scaled, not the comp's type sitting inside a wider layout.
Every spacing and text value is a token (--space-N, --text-N); raw px in a component rule is a wall violation (webui-css-tokens-only).

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: Color is never decorative. A holder edge is the only place attention is carried by color, it always ships with a text label, and there is no second accent anywhere else in the frame — a former vermilion/cinnabar accent is the one pigment the world forbids by name.

rules.name: The Own-Ground-Own-Ink Rule
rules.body: Every plane declares its own ink and a shared label inherits it (color: inherit) rather than hard-coding a room ink into a primitive that also prints on paper.

rules.name: The Plane-Measured Contrast Rule
rules.body: Hairline and mute-ink strengths are allowed to differ between the dark and light themes because each is measured against its own ground to the same target band, not equalized numerically.

rules.name: The One Size Rule
rules.body: A Figure is one size at any call site; what marks a value as a figure is the tabular numeral face, never a size jump.

rules.name: The Regular-Weight Rule
rules.body: Strip labels and strip values are weight 400, not bold, measured against the comp's own recorded regular-weight text regions.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default, Ink-Not-Light Rule
rules.body: No radius, no ambient drop shadow anywhere in the room. Depth is stacked hairline rings mixed against the exact plane they sit on, never a box-shadow blur simulating a light source.

dos: Do keep every color, spacing and type value bound to a token (--space-1..--space-8, --text-1..--text-6, the section-1 palette tokens); the webui-css-tokens-only wall fails a raw px or hex in a component rule.
Do carry state exclusively through the four holder-edge colors, each always paired with a text label.
Do measure a new plane's ink and border against the exact background it prints on, and record the reading in a comment, the way every existing token in tokens.css does.
Do keep radius at 0 and depth as tonal plane plus hairline everywhere.
Do use the tabular figure face for anything that lines up in a column; use the mute label face for captions; use the monospace face only for genuinely monospace content.
donts: Don't introduce a second accent color. The room's holder edges and the focus blue are the whole of its chroma.
Don't build a hero-metric tile (a value at a jumped-up size over a small unit and basis); this system rejects the KPI-tile dashboard of the category.
Don't add a card-and-shadow surface, a sparkline, a progress ring, or a soft-shadowed rounded rectangle standing in for real content.
Don't use a dashed-box, centered-text empty state; an empty rack prints as a strip carrying no data.
Don't reintroduce a floating popover/menu layer with a z-index stack; this world's options print in flow.

Don't invent a kicker or eyebrow label, a hard-offset neobrutalist shadow, a system display face, or a Unicode/emoji glyph standing in for an icon — none appear in the shipped build and none should be added to extend the system.
